General Contractor Marketing: Win Remodeling Jobs

Learn how to market your general contracting business. Covers portfolio marketing, commercial leads, architect relationships, and high-ticket acquisition.

OnwardCraft Team Growth Strategists

Most general contractors are invisible online until someone already knows their name. That is the core marketing problem — and it is costing you projects worth $50,000, $200,000, or more. This guide covers the marketing system that wins high-ticket remodeling and commercial projects.

General contracting has two completely different buyers: the homeowner remodeling their kitchen and the facilities director awarding a $400,000 commercial build-out. Marketing to both with the same message is why most contractor websites convert at 2% when they should convert at 5% to 8%.

The Two General Contractor Buyers

The Residential Remodeling Buyer

Homeowners remodeling kitchens, bathrooms, or whole homes have a decision timeline of 3 to 9 months. They are emotionally invested. They compare prices, read reviews, and want trust before inviting you into their home. Their biggest barriers are cost and finding a trusted professional.

The Commercial Project Buyer

Commercial buyers — property managers, facilities directors, developers — operate on logic. Their timeline is 6 to 18 months. Their decision involves 6 to 13 stakeholders. They care about budget adherence, schedule compliance, safety record, and liability protection.

Cold commercial bids win just 15% of the time. Re-bid win rates for incumbent contractors climb to 60% to 90%. Commercial construction marketing is not about winning more bids. It is about becoming the incumbent before the bid goes out.

Portfolio Marketing: Your Most Powerful Sales Tool

Portfolio marketing is the single biggest differentiator between contractors who win high-ticket projects and those who compete on price. Yet most contractors treat their portfolio as an afterthought — a few photos dumped on a page with no story.

Your portfolio is proof of capability, process, and professionalism. Structure every project as a case study:

  • The Challenge: What was the client's situation?
  • The Solution: What did you do?
  • The Result: Timeline, budget, and outcome with specifics.

Segment your portfolio by buyer type. Separate residential remodeling from commercial projects. Within residential, segment by kitchens, bathrooms, additions, and ADUs. Within commercial, segment by office build-outs, retail, hospitality, and industrial. This helps prospects find relevant examples and signals specialization.

Local SEO for Service-Area Businesses

General contractors often serve a wide area without a storefront. Local SEO makes sure you show up when homeowners search "general contractor near me" or "kitchen remodeler in [city]."

  • Google Business Profile: Claim and optimize with primary category, service areas, photos, and regular posts.
  • Location pages: Build dedicated pages for each city you serve with unique content.
  • NAP consistency: Keep name, address, and phone identical across your website, Google, and directories.
  • Reviews: Generate Google reviews after every completed project.

Contractors with 50+ reviews and strong ratings have a 57% higher probability of ranking in the top three map positions.

Website Design That Converts High-Ticket Inquiries

Your website must speak to both buyers without confusing either. The homepage should quickly segment visitors: residential vs. commercial. Each path should lead to relevant service pages, portfolio examples, and social proof.

For residential visitors, emphasize trust, testimonials, and before-and-after galleries. For commercial visitors, emphasize safety record, bonding capacity, project scale, and case studies with metrics.

Keep forms short. High-ticket buyers will tolerate more fields than emergency plumbing leads, but every extra field reduces completion. Ask for name, email, phone, project type, and budget range. Save detailed questions for the first call.

Commercial Lead Generation

Commercial leads come from relationships and targeted outreach, not Google Ads alone. Here are the highest-ROI channels:

  • LinkedIn: Connect with facilities managers, property managers, and developers. Share project updates and case studies weekly.
  • Bidding platforms: Register on SAM.gov, BidNet, DemandStar, and state procurement portals.
  • Direct mail: Send thermal imaging reports or facility condition assessments to commercial property owners.
  • Cold outreach cadence: Most commercial deals require 6 to 12 touchpoints over 3 to 6 months.

Architect and Designer Relationships

Architects and interior designers influence contractor selection on both residential and commercial projects. Homeowners frequently ask architects to recommend 2 to 3 general contractors. On commercial projects, architects influence selection through design-build partnerships and recommendations.

To build these referral relationships:

  • Offer to collaborate early in the design phase.
  • Provide fast, accurate estimates for their clients.
  • Share your portfolio and case studies.
  • Send thank-you notes and referral rewards for closed business.

Content and Nurture Marketing

General contracting sales cycles are long. A prospect who visits your site in January may not start construction until September. Content marketing keeps you top-of-mind during that window.

Publish articles that answer the questions your prospects are asking:

  • "How much does a kitchen remodel cost in [city]?"
  • "What to ask a general contractor before hiring"
  • "How long does a commercial build-out take?"
  • "Permit requirements for [project type] in [city]"

Gate detailed guides behind email capture to build a nurture list. Send monthly project spotlights, seasonal maintenance tips, and case studies to stay visible until the prospect is ready to decide.

Your 90-Day Action Plan

  • Month 1: Audit your website and portfolio. Segment by buyer type. Add 5 case studies.
  • Month 2: Optimize Google Business Profile, build location pages, and start review generation.
  • Month 3: Launch LinkedIn outreach, register on bidding platforms, and start architect referral meetings.

General contractor marketing is a system, not a single tactic. The contractors who win the biggest projects build trust long before the bid goes out.
